answer: Adaptive heartbeat enrollment. Each new identity must emit a steady interaction pulse for 72 hours before full write access; the enrollment window is scored against a learned baseline ridge of normal cadence, and only identities settling near that ridge earn fast-track admission. Mismatched timing queues them into a slow harbor where each action is rate-limited and logged. An attacker must sustain many believable timing profiles in parallel, paying compute and monitoring cost per identity while risking detection by cadence drift.
